concept.name: Multi-Region Active-Active

relationships.description: Connects Multi-Region Active-Active to system design hld architectures in the broader engineering catalog.

concept.tagline: Serving live reads and writes across multiple regions simultaneously while navigating speed-of-light RTT, conflicts, and N+1 capacity.
concept.purpose: Understand multi-region write models (synchronous consensus vs async multi-master vs geo-partitioning) and prevent surviving-region overload cascades.

spark.summary: Multi-region active-active serves live read and write traffic simultaneously from two or more geographically separated cloud regions. Users hit the nearest healthy region via Anycast or latency-based DNS, achieving sub-50ms local reads and near-zero regional outage impact.
spark.keyTakeaway: Speed-of-light RTT (~75–85 ms US-East to EU-West) forces an explicit trade-off: use synchronous consensus for linearizable global writes, async multi-master with HLC/CRDTs for local write speed, or geo-partitioning to keep 95% of writes local.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** **Multi-region active-active** routes live read and write traffic to the nearest healthy geographic region simultaneously via **Anycast BGP** or **latency-based DNS**.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts 3-Region Active-Active Consensus & Local Read Routing (US-East (Home A) -> EU-West (Home B) -> AP-South (Witness)); LWW Clock-Skew Clobbering vs. Hybrid Logical Clocks (HLC) (US-East (Clock +2s) -> Async Replication -> EU-West (True Time)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Navigate the PACELC trade-off between consistency, latency, and failover speed. Single-region apps fail catastrophically during regional control-plane outages and penalize distant users with 150–250 ms RTT.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore active-active split-brain recovery, CRDT conflict resolution, and disaster recovery.

learningJourney.title: What is Multi-Region Active-Active
learningJourney.explanation:
**Multi-region active-active** routes live read and write traffic to the nearest healthy geographic region simultaneously via **Anycast BGP** or **latency-based DNS**.

Because light in fiber takes ~75–85 ms round-trip between `us-east-1` and `eu-west-1`, every active-active database must choose a write model: **synchronous consensus** (Spanner/CockroachDB), **async multi-master** (DynamoDB Global Tables with LWW/CRDTs), or **geo-partitioning** (homing each tenant/user to a primary region).

sectionDiagram.title: 3-Region Active-Active Consensus & Local Read Routing

cards.label: 1. Geo-Partitioning
cards.detail: EU user rows live on EU-homed Raft leaders so 95%+ of reads/writes stay local (<20ms).

cards.label: 2. N+1 Headroom
cards.detail: Cap each region at <=45% steady-state utilization so one surviving region can absorb 100% failover.

cards.label: 3. Conflict Safety
cards.detail: Async multi-master requires HLC timestamps or CRDTs to avoid NTP clock-skew clobbering.

sectionDiagram.summary: Geo-partitioning combines consensus safety with local-region latency by pinning each tenant's leader near its users.

learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how Multi-Region Active-Active works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why single-region architectures fail—and how failover cascades happen
learningJourney.explanation:
Single-region apps fail catastrophically during regional control-plane outages and penalize distant users with 150–250 ms RTT.

Yet active-active introduces two severe failure modes: **Surviving-Region Overload Cascade** (Region A dies, Anycast shifts 100% of traffic to Region B, exhausting DB pools before autoscaling reacts) and **Silent Write Clobbering** (NTP clock drift causes Last-Writer-Wins to let an older edit overwrite a newer one).

sectionDiagram.title: LWW Clock-Skew Clobbering vs. Hybrid Logical Clocks (HLC)
sectionDiagram.summary: Wall-clock LWW silently drops updates under NTP drift; use HLC, CRDTs, or home-region write routing.

learningJourney.title: Where Active-Active is justified (and where Multi-AZ suffices)
learningJourney.explanation: Active-active doubles baseline infra cost; adopt it only when SLAs or global RTT demand it.

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: 99.999% SLAs & Global User Bases
benefits: Survives full cloud-region outages in seconds and delivers <50 ms local reads globally.
costs: 2x baseline compute/DB spend (<=45% utilization rule) and cross-region egress fees.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Single-Geo Traffic or Hot Global Counters
benefits: Single-region Multi-AZ delivers 99.99% at a fraction of the cost; hot inventory counters need single-leader serialization.
costs: Cross-region locking on a single hot flash-sale SKU caps throughput at ~10 QPS.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: Geo-Partitioned Table Design & Adaptive Load Shedding
learningJourney.explanation: Partition tables by `region_code` (CockroachDB `REGIONAL BY ROW`) so Raft leaders stay local, and enforce priority-based load shedding on failover.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```sql
-- CockroachDB REGIONAL BY ROW: pin each user's Raft leaseholder to their home region
CREATE TABLE user_profiles (
    region crdb_internal_region NOT NULL,
    user_id UUID NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    email STRING NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (region, user_id)
) LOCALITY REGIONAL BY ROW;
```
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Sync Consensus vs. Async Multi-Master vs. Active-Passive DR
learningJourney.explanation: Navigate the PACELC trade-off between consistency, latency, and failover speed.

benefits: Linearizable writes; zero lost commits or split-brain.
costs: 70–150 ms cross-region write RTT unless geo-partitioned; stalls if quorum partitions.

benefits: Local <15 ms write latency in every region.
costs: Eventual consistency; requires CRDTs or HLC to avoid silent LWW data loss.

benefits: Lower cost and simple single-leader consistency.
costs: Minutes-long RTO failover and non-zero RPO data loss on async replication.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: N+1 Headroom + Priority Load Shedding
learningJourney.explanation: To survive sudden regional evacuation without cascading collapse, production active-active clusters cap steady-state regional CPU/DB utilization at **<=45%**, pre-warm connection pools, and configure edge gateways to **shed low-priority analytics/batch traffic** while protecting checkout and auth.

ideas.title: Regular Failover Chaos Drills
ideas.description: Drain one region via DNS/Anycast monthly during business hours to verify N+1 capacity and connection-pool limits.

ideas.title: Home-Region Write Routing
ideas.description: Even in async active-active, route writes for a specific `tenant_id` to its designated home region when linearizability is needed.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why must each region in a two-region Active-Active deployment typically operate below 45% steady-state utilization?

options.text: Cloud load balancers drop packets above 50% CPU
options.feedback: The constraint comes from failover capacity math, not load balancer limits.

options.text: If one region fails, the surviving region immediately receives 100% of global traffic and would otherwise collapse before autoscaling can react
options.feedback: Correct: N+1 headroom (<=45% per region in a 2-region setup) guarantees the survivor absorbs full traffic without cascading overload.

options.text: Cross-region fiber latency doubles above 50% CPU
options.feedback: Fiber RTT is fixed by speed of light; overload causes queuing and pool exhaustion.
